Morgan Stanley: Net new assets (NNA) represent client asset inflows, inclusive of interest, dividends and asset acquisitions, less client asset outflows, and exclude the impact of business combinations/divestitures and the impact of fees and commissions.

The Charles Schwab Corporation: Net new client assets are total inflows of client cash and securities to Schwab less client outflows; inflows include dividends and interest, outflows include commissions and fees, and capital gains distributions are excluded.

The Charles Schwab Corporation: Core net new client assets are net new client assets before significant one-time inflows or outflows, such as acquisitions/divestitures or extraordinary flows (generally greater than $25 billion, $10 billion prior to 2025) relating to a specific client, and activity from off-platform brokered CDs issued by CSB.
Edward Jones: Net new assets represents cash and securities inflows and outflows, including fees and commissions and excluding mutual fund capital gain distributions received by U.S. clients.
Edward Jones (in its 2025 annual report): Net new assets represents cash and securities inflows and outflows, excluding mutual fund capital gain distributions received by U.S. clients.

Merrill: Within Bank of America's Global Wealth & Investment Management segment, net new assets (its net client AUM flows) are defined as the net change in clients' AUM balances over a specified period of time, excluding market appreciation/depreciation and other adjustments.

Raymond James Financial: Domestic Private Client Group net new assets represents domestic PCG client inflows, including dividends and interest, less domestic PCG client outflows, including commissions, advisory fees, and other fees.
